summary.text: 从 is a two-person picture: one person follows another. This construction supports the sense ‘follow’; early uses are also reported with the meaning ‘from’.

formation.text: Pictographic compound: two 人 figures depict people arranged one after another. Their relation contributes the idea of following; neither figure is a movement marker or sound cue in 从.

components.text: 人 is the visible form of each figure. In this character, both figures are pictorial: together they depict one person following another. No separate earlier form is established for either component.
人 is the visible form of the second figure. Alongside the first 人, it completes the reported scene of one person following another; it has no independent sound role here.

history.text: The graph is reported in oracle-bone and bronze materials. Curated oracle-style and seal-style depictions retain a pair of human figures; the seal-style form regularizes their arrangement. These images illustrate the reported analysis and do not establish a direct sequence between the pictured forms.

The later graph 從 adds 辵 in the historical dictionary’s analysis. That account treats 辵 as movement-related and 从 as phonetic; the added element marks a different graph construction, not a component of current 从.

uncertainties.text: The two-person interpretation is a reported analysis; the underlying inscription images were not visually inspected in this research. The dossier does not fix the earliest absolute date of the graph or of each reported sense.

The historical dictionary gives 从 and 從 separate entries, while a later editorial account treats ‘heed/obey’ and ‘follow/accompany’ as related by extension and sees the separation as reflecting later usage. The dossier does not resolve this difference or establish a complete chronology linking the reported meanings.

senses.period: dating unresolved; reported in oracle-bone and bronze materials
senses.text: The two-person picture is interpreted as one person following another. This is the earliest meaning supported by the reported graph analysis, though the exact earliest dated occurrence is not established.

senses.period: oracle-bone uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Oracle-bone uses of 从 are reported with ‘from’ senses, including examples glossed ‘from the west’ and ‘from the east’. Their relation in time to the ‘follow’ use is not established.

senses.period: Han dictionary account; earlier chronology unresolved
senses.text: The Han dictionary glosses 从 as ‘heed’ and analyzes it as two 人. A later editorial interpretation connects this sense with ‘follow/accompany’ by extension, but the historical transition is not securely dated.

senses.period: bronze uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples are reported for 从 meaning ‘follow’ and for 從 meaning ‘accompany’. The evidence does not establish a complete sequence among these uses and the other reported senses.

senses.gloss: indulge (written with 從 as a loan for 縱)
senses.period: bronze use reported; exact date unresolved
senses.text: A bronze use of 從 is reported as a loan spelling for 縱 ‘indulge’: the written graph was reused for a different word, rather than the graph’s meaning developing into ‘indulge’. The source word’s sound comparison and the borrowing’s date are not established here.
These are supplied modern glosses for 从. The dossier does not establish how or when each developed from earlier uses.

developments.text: A later editorial account relates ‘follow/accompany’ and ‘heed/obey’ by semantic extension, while the Han dictionary treats 从 and 從 as separate entries. The evidence does not settle the development.
Both uses are reported for early material, but the dossier supplies no dated chain showing that ‘from’ developed from ‘follow’.

limitations.text: The reported uses do not establish a secure absolute chronology or a complete semantic chain. Modern glosses alone cannot show how ‘from’, ‘since’, ‘through’, or ‘by’ arose.
No graph-loan source word or sound match for 从/從 is established in the dossier. Tentative proposed comparisons are unverified and do not support a borrowing account.

overview.text: 从 pictures two people, one following the other. This makes ‘follow’ the clearest explanation of the whole character; ‘from’ is also reported in early use, but its development is not established.

components.text: This 人 is pictured as one of the two people in the following scene.
This 人 is pictured as the other person in the scene; together, the pair conveys following.
